readability_observation.observed_local_repairs: The candidate joins fragmented opening lines, fixes several classifiers and malformed attachments, replaces a context-supported token mistranslation, removes doubled framing, and adds three paragraph boundaries while preserving the long-article format. These are visible editing changes, not measured improvements in willingness to continue reading.
remaining_problems: The editorial summary and the interview sometimes differ in qualification or metric, including the AGI bottleneck framing and user-versus-usage growth. A fluency repair does not resolve their evidential relationship.
The unlabeled apparent interviewer paragraph remains an attribution obstacle. Correcting it would require source support, not a guessed speaker.

The model/API/framework and proactive-teammate explanations recur at length, and the Atlas/Sora acceleration accounts repeat with somewhat different details. Any structural compression would need a detail-level inventory to retain distinct anecdotes and milestones.

The source phrase about Branded Codebase and the repeated shifts among models, products, and brands remain difficult to interpret from the Chinese text alone. They should remain flagged rather than silently normalized to a guessed proper name.
Some long paragraphs and mixed-language expressions remain; the small number of paragraph splits does not establish that the whole interview is easy to follow.
readability_observation.possible_next_work: A separately versioned revision could first preserve the disputed qualifier and keep the uncertain interpretations explicitly unresolved. A further structure pass could map repeated themes and distinct supporting details before changing organization. Reader benefit would require a whole-article comparison and human evidence.
